invariants: Skill is an adapter, not a Story OS copy.
Canonical engine exists only under episodes/_system.
Evidence files never become a second stage source.
Reality constrains capture behavior, not concept scale or fictional world existence.
Environment is a physical contract, not a visual filter.
Resolved Frame Contracts are derived caches; Story, Storyboard, story-gates and Visual Profile remain authoritative.
Large anomaly scale is not a Visual Lock failure by itself; capture credibility and promised impact are judged separately.
Image workers may run concurrently, but Production Ledger mutations remain single-writer.
Maximum supported formal image concurrency is 3.
Fast Frame Scout may request repair but never authorizes final Production PASS.
Final Candidate Snapshot is evidence, not a second creative authority.
V2.1 Delivery Adapter must consume a verified snapshot instead of rescanning mutable publish files.
Legacy episodes are never upgraded by fabricating V2.1 PASS evidence.
Post-publish facts and metrics must not mutate the frozen release manifest.
Post-publish learning is evidence for the next story, never direct creative authority.
DATA_REVIEWED uses the canonical episode-state.json stage; no second stage system exists.
Runtime Request captures user intent/execution parameters and never becomes creative authority.
Missing user plot means auto_create; Story OS must author the story instead of asking for a plot.
A rough user plot is a seed to strengthen and rewrite, not an automatic Story Lock.
Image model defaults to gpt-image-2 when the user does not specify one.
An explicitly requested image model must not be silently substituted.
Current V2.1 Visual Lock is exactly four admission images; three-image wording is legacy-only.
Runtime DAG is execution evidence only and never a second episode state machine.
Completed valid stage targets are reused on resume instead of rerunning the whole Codex supervisor.
Warm image worker pool reuses Python process/module state only; Codex conversation state remains isolated until a safe persistent transport exists.
Plus/Codex quota percentages are never guessed; automatic telemetry records only observable counters.
Continuous image scheduling removes wave barriers but preserves max3 image workers and single-writer ledger semantics.
Rolling pre-final review can trigger early repair but can never grant final frame PASS.
Provisional release material is runtime-only and can never mutate frozen release authority.
Default protagonists are ordinary young people, not occupational tools invented to solve the anomaly.
Casual work/research/expedition may explain arrival but must not turn the protagonist into an anomaly-solving professional.
First-person POV still requires a stable Character Contract.
Character Contract is a Story Build input and never a second Episode stage.
New Story runs must pass NO-ANOMALY TEST and Character Contract validation before STORYBOARD_LOCKED.
Resolved Frame Contract binds Character Contract so character drift invalidates downstream cache.
preproduction_only never invokes image generation.
image_continue must verify handoff authority hashes and must not rewrite locked Story.
shared resource library reuses references/descriptors, never prior final episode images by default.
intro templates are structural references and must be naturally rewritten.
title is one internal candidate and is not a PUBLISH_READY requirement.
V2.2 Visual Narrative Core formal production activation is based on Episode tool_version >= 2.2.0, never mere file presence.
Legacy Episode regression inputs are NON_AUTHORITY_REGRESSION_ONLY and can never become production authority by implication.
A missing or zero-frame V2.2 Visual Narrative input can never PASS verification.
Legacy Episode final or Visual Lock reviews must not inherit V2.2-only checks unless the Episode itself is formally V2.2+.
Story OS 2.2.1 defaults to Mainland China, Chinese local residents and ordinary Chinese young adults unless the Episode explicitly overrides World Identity.
Default Chinese context constrains national/cultural context, not a single ethnicity; natural Chinese regional and ethnic diversity remains valid.
Episode World Identity overrides are explicit and replace/inherit defaults deterministically.
Character Appearance Anchor is a derived cache and never replaces Character Contract, Character Visual Contract or Visual Lock pixel master.
World Identity and Character Appearance Anchor bind Resolved Frame Contract hashes for V2.2.1+ Episodes.
V2.2.0 and earlier Episodes do not inherit V2.2.1-only pixel review checks retroactively.
legacy_adapter_note: Legacy repository adapter paths may keep historical names; product/system name is Story OS.
